title: Finite coefficient constant models and finite stalk constructibility
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme and $A$ a finite commutative ring with its discrete condensed structure. On the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], identify the pulled-back coefficient ring $p_X^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$, and internal modules with ordinary module sheaves, by [lem-sf-module-object-ordinary-coefficient-equivalence]. A module sheaf is constructible in the finite constant local model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible] if and only if its corresponding ordinary $A_X$-module sheaf is constructible in the locally constant finite-stalk sense of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf]. The same finite constructible locally closed stratifications and trivializing covers can be used, after discarding empty covering objects. Consequently the induced equivalence identifies the bounded constructible derived subcategories, with exactly the same cohomological vanishing intervals.

source.place: Second paragraph: the finite-stalk constructibility convention used for all quotient coefficients.

proof.text: Choose the normalized Encoding E_T for every scheme T. The proved normalized pullback comparison identifies the encoded internal pullback with fixed-module inverse image. The intrinsic restriction/pullback comparison then gives the corresponding intrinsic ordinary module.

The scalar-model comparison identifies finitely presented scalar constant extensions with finite constant fixed-module sheaves, on each original covering arrow. The fully faithful intrinsic scalar restriction reflects these constant-model isomorphisms, proving the same-cover clause.

The scalar-model comparison and normalized pullback identify internal finite-model covers with ordinary small finite-model covers. Reindexing small covers upward and shrinking an arbitrary cover downward identifies these with fixed-module finite local constancy. The existing intrinsic finite-local-constancy comparison identifies this with local constancy and finite geometric stalks.

Apply the local comparison after normalized pullback to each fixed stratum. On a Noetherian scheme the internal definition is its global stratified branch. The existing intrinsic/fixed constructibility comparison handles the positive-strata convention, including the empty scheme.

Delete the empty members from an arbitrary ordinary trivializing cover. They contribute neither points nor affine open subsets, so both the jointly-surjective and quasi-compact covering conditions persist. On a nonempty member choose a geometric point using an algebraic closure of its residue field. Slice stalk comparison identifies the constant value with the fixed geometric stalk, and intrinsic/fixed scalar restriction transports the assumed finiteness.

The weakly etale slice equivalence sends each retained localized constant model to a constant model on the source scheme. Normalized pullback and the scalar-model comparison produce the required finitely presented internal scalar model on exactly that member.

The exact ordinary equivalence commutes with every derived homology functor and preserves and reflects zero homology and boundedness. The sheaf comparison identifies constructibility in each degree. Restrict its actual derived equivalence to the two full bounded-constructible subcategories; closure under isomorphism gives the ambient-functor commuting isomorphism.

Against the live side node, only the proof fields, split_report and the Mathlib searches changed; the statement and stmt_deps are unchanged. There are no new nodes, no cycle (closure of 735 nodes), no node from the dropped list and no SGA. The item comes from Q34's re-split of its parent; no re-split note targets the item itself. Step checks: (1) the coefficient equivalence is the canonical κ_T one, it keeps the underlying abelian sheaves, and lem-sfb-internal-module-operations-transport gives compatibility with pullback to strata and to covering objects. (2) Over a finite ring A, finitely presented is the same as finite as a set (A^P→P, finite kernel R, A^R→A^P); I tested A=0 and A=Z/4 with P=Z/2. (3) The scalar local model Λ_U⊗_{Λ(*)_U}P_U is just P_U, with explicit inverse maps. (4) lem-weil-pbc-proetale-finite-model-stalks gives finite geometric stalks on the same cover. (5) For the converse, discarding empty covering objects keeps an fpqc cover, and this clause is genuinely needed: the constant sheaf of an infinite module on an empty object is zero. On each remaining object a geometric point plus inverse-image-restriction, inverse-image-stalk and constant-sheaf-stalk show each P_i is finite, on the original cover. (6) Both definitions use the same stratifications; empty strata impose nothing. (7) The exact equivalence commutes with H^q and the inverse equivalence reflects vanishing, so the bounded constructible subcategories correspond with the same vanishing intervals. Duplicate search: the existing constructible comparisons (classicality, étale versus pro-étale, adic locally-finitely-presented versus local model, the curves case) do not state this one. The 6 declared tool uses are generic and accepted.
